newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul backs $5.64/shr 1997 oper EPS view.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul backs $5.64/shr 1997 oper EPS view.

text.p: St. Paul Cos Chief Executive Douglas Leatherdale said Tuesday that analysts' estimates calling for earnings a share of $5.64 from continuing operations for 1997 are "in the ballpark."

"Assuming we have reasonably normal catastrophic losses, we will return from last year's depressed results to our traditional level of profitability, which is about a 13 percent return on beginning equity," he told Reuters following the insurance company's annnual meeting here. "So I would not disagree with the range around that consensus (of $5.64)."
The company reported earnings of $4.55 a share from continuing operations in 1996.
Leatherdale reiterated Tuesday that the company expected to report pretax catastrophic losses of $30 million to $40 million from flooding in the Red River Valley.
In comments to shareholders, Leatherdale said the company "will seize opportunities to acquire complimentary business... in the coming months and years."
After the meeting, Leatherdale told Reuters that reinsurance companies and companies offering commercial insurance lines would be among primary acquisition targets.

"The things that interest us most are the reinsurance business and the commercial kinds of businesses," he said. "As opposed to personal lines, we would tend to focus on commercial, and that may mean everything from medical practice to construction coverge for contractors."
Leatherdale also said he expected the company's reinsurance revenues would be little changed in 1997 from 1996.

"That business is very competitive and costumers are buying less reinsurance," Leatherdale said. "They have more capital and they are maintaining more of the risk themselves. As a result, we expect our reinsurance revenues to be rather flat in 1997 versus 1996." The company reported $761 million in written premiums from reinsurance in 1996.
He also said international underwriting, which made up six percent of written premiums in 1996, would be the company's fastest growing business line.

"The area that will grow the most rapidly will be the international side, that's where we're placing a great deal of emphasis," he said. "Over the next five years, that six percent share of premiums would certainly double."
St. Paul Cos shares closed up 3/4 at 70-3/4 Tuesday.
